subject: Console inspector: economics debugging playbook request & SLA-exception signals
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tom Harper <tom.harper@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Console inspector: economics debugging playbook request & SLA-exception signals

Team and Tom —

Following our support run yesterday with Acme I wanted to capture a concrete ask for the Console/Inspector surface that would make diagnosing cost+latency SLA exceptions a lot faster for both CS and the customer. Acme ran into a sequence where tail-latency and token spend spiked concurrently on a small set of routes, and we had to stitch traces across three dashboards and two ad-hoc queries.

High-level request: build a short, opinionated "economics debugging" playbook inside the Inspector that surfaces per-route breakdowns and the minimal telemetry needed to triage SLA exceptions. Goal is to cut time-to-root-cause under 20 minutes for common cases.

Must-haves (MVP):
- Tile: Per-route cost vs 95/99 latency (last 1h, 24h, 7d) with percent change and top contributing models/variants.
- Quicklinks: link to last N traces / sample request payloads (sampled at 1%) and associated KV-cache hit rate.
- Signal checklist: sampling rate, sequence length distribution, batching window, quantization profile in use.
- Owner attribution: which infra/owner last rolled model/variant for the route (from rollout metadata).

Nice-to-have: anomaly hints (token path anomalies), automatically suggested rollback candidate (compatible variant with lower cost) based on historical unit economics.

Ask of this thread: can Platform (Irene, Rishi) and Product (Marissa) agree on a minimal data contract and acceptance criteria? I attached a rough mock and a short schema snippet to start the wire-up.

Proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
1) Tile renders for any route with >1k calls/day.
2) Cost and latency series are aligned on the same aggregation window and annotated with sample rate.
3) Inspector surfaces at least one trace and one sampled request payload for the window.
4) Playbook shows a suggested owner and a rollback candidate when a model variant created within 7 days has 10%+ cost delta.

Scheduling: if we can align on data contract today, can engineering scope an MVP for the end of sprint (2 weeks)?

Thanks —
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Product Manager, Console & Observability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: console-inspector-mock.png (PNG, 240kb), data-schema-snippet.json (JSON, 2kb)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc:
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Console inspector: economics debugging playbook request & SLA-exception signals

Thanks for the concise brief, Jasmine — this is the right direction. A few quick notes from infra/telemetry POV:

- Data sources: we need to agree whether the Inspector will consume (a) pre-aggregated per-route metrics (existing metrics service), or (b) a near-real-time sample stream + on-the-fly aggregation. Both have tradeoffs: pre-agg gives stability but lags; stream gives freshness but costs more. For SLA exceptions freshness matters.
- Traces: we can link to TRACE IDs in our trace system. Need a standard naming convention so the UI can fetch them automatically.
- Sampling: current default request sampling is 0.5% in production; recommend 1% for routes with SLA breach or >50% cost delta.

I can work with Rishi to sketch the minimal metric contract and a pragmatic fallback (pre-agg with 1min rollups + sampled stream). Rishi — can you confirm what the impact is on ingestion and any additional tags needed (model_variant, rollout_id, tenant_id, route_id, sample_rate)?

Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Engineering Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 12:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Console inspector: economics debugging playbook request & SLA-exception signals

Quick technical reply with feasibility notes:

- Aggregation/latency windows: we can provide 1m/5m/1h rollups for cost and latency. Align UI windows to these buckets to avoid confusion.
- Sampled payloads/traces: we can bump to 1% sampling on routes flagged by the Inspector. Cost impact estimated ~+0.6% ingestion for those routes; acceptable if scope limited to incidents.
- Required tags: route_id (string), tenant_id, model_family, model_variant, rollout_id, seq_len_bucket (<=128, 129-512, >512), batch_size_bucket, kv_cache_hit=true/false.
- KV-cache hit rate: we can emit per-variant kv_hit_rate metric at 1m granularity. Note: for quantized variants we sometimes see higher latent variance depending on kernel choice — we should display variant-level latency distribution, not only percentiles.

Roadmap/timebox idea:
- Week 0: finalize data contract (metrics + sampling behavior) — this thread.
- Week 1: infra exposes endpoints (1m rollups + sample fetcher).
- Week 2: UI tile and trace link integration (MVP).

I'll open an implementation ticket (OBS-1129) with the contract. Irene — can you own the infra ticket? Jasmine/Marissa — confirm UX acceptance criteria and whether we want auto-trigger rules for sampling on breach.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Console inspector: economics debugging playbook request & SLA-exception signals

Thanks all — good alignment. Quick summary and next steps so we have a single owner list: 

Action items:
- Irene: own OBS-1129, expose 1m rollups + sample fetcher, ensure tags (route_id, tenant_id, model_variant, rollout_id) are available. (ETA: 1 week)
- Rishi: detail the metric schema and attach ingestion cost estimate to OBS-1129. (ETA: 48 hours)
- Jasmine: finalize UX acceptance criteria and update the doc (linked). I'll help prioritize the tile in Product sprint. (ETA: EOD Monday)
- Marissa: I will coordinate CS validation with Acme and prepare a short checklist CS can follow during incidents.

If we hit the acceptance criteria Jasmine outlined, we should be able to get the MVP into a limited rollout with Acme within 3 weeks.

Marissa Cole
Product Lead, Observability
Redwood Inference
